environment_constraints: NO DEPLOY: no lambda update-function-code, no version publish, no alias move. AWS READS are expected and fine (profile wecare-prod, account 775261844268, us-east-1, already exported via AWS_PROFILE). NEVER call `aws secretsmanager get-secret-value` or `batch-get-secret-value` in any spelling - a PreToolUse hook blocks it. Never put a credential, token or OTP on a command line. contribution_requirements: Single-branch workflow: commit directly to `stack`, never create a branch, NEVER push (this task is explicitly no-push). The git index is SHARED with other live sessions and was dirty at planning time (amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/ecommerce/order_creation.py, amplify/infra/checkout.json, scripts/provision_checkout.py, tests/test_checkout_package_completeness.py, tests/test_provision_checkout_contract.py all modified by another workstream). Therefore `git commit --only <explicit paths> -F <message-file>` is MANDATORY, not optional - a plain `git add && git commit` will absorb another session's files. Untracked new files need `git add <new paths>` first, then `git commit --only <all paths>`. Never `git add .` / -A / -u (hook-blocked). No force push, no history rewrite, no stash, no fetch/reset/rebase.
key_patterns: Handlers are thin wiring over pure, AWS-free, storage-agnostic modules in lambda_utils; every side effect is injected so the ordering is testable (see identity/registration.py). Exceptions log type(exc).__name__ only, never the message - CodeQL py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data tracks taint across function boundaries and has failed this build twice, including on a ternary that could not leak. Phone numbers are masked to last-4 in logs. Secrets are read lazily at request time by SecretId reference inside the Lambda, never at module scope. Modules carry long docstrings that explain WHY a decision was taken and record rejected alternatives - match that density. Behaviour-pinning tests sometimes walk the AST rather than the text (see tests/test_payment_vocabulary_at_decision_points.py) because the explanatory comments necessarily contain the forbidden literal.
